q1-collapse-501-468.title: Do #501 and #468 describe the same defect, judged from their bodies?
q1-collapse-501-468.imperative: NOT OVERRIDABLE pre-ruling 3: confirm the collapse against the issue BODY, not the title. Quote the passage in each body that names the same mechanism, and name anything one body asks for that the other does not — a partial overlap is not a collapse.
q1-collapse-501-468.finding:
COLLAPSE HOLDS on the primary defect, verified against both BODIES.

#501 body: "The guard exists to assert *you are running from an installed skill directory*. The repository is itself named constellation-skills, so from a repo checkout skill_root.name is constellation-skills, startswith("constellation-") is True, the guard passes, and the function returns C:/Programs as the skills root."

#468 body: "From the vendored copy, parents[1] is the repo root, whose name is constellation-skills -- which starts with constellation-. So the guard passes on the one input it was written to reject, then derives a sibling-skills root of C:\Programs\ and fails downstream with a path that looks like a broken install."

Same function (_installed_skills_root), same line (scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py:53), same predicate, same wrong-root consequence, and both classify it explicitly as the check-that-cannot-fail class.

PARTIAL OVERLAP NOTED, so the collapse is not total: #501 carries a SECOND defect that #468 never mentions -- "verify_admiral_prelaunch reads NEXT_WAVE.json for its boundary_id. That file persists from the previous boundary, so running the check before writing the new one re-validates the boundary that already passed and reports ok." That sits in #501's Suggested Fix (item 3), NOT in its Acceptance, so #501's stated acceptance can be met without it. Carried to q12 as an explicit scope decision rather than silently dropped.

q2-collapse-439-484.title: Do #439 and #484 describe the same defect, judged from their bodies?
q2-collapse-439-484.imperative: Same rule as q1. Quote from each body. Note where their SUGGESTED FIXES diverge, since a shared defect with two proposed mechanisms still collapses.
q2-collapse-439-484.finding:
COLLAPSE HOLDS, verified against both BODIES.

#439 body: "<branch> is never resolved ... is not among them and is left as a literal string in the materialized spine.json. At advance archive the engine runs gh pr list --head "<branch>" ... verbatim, which matches no real branch and always returns an empty list, so c2b always fails".

#484 body: "<branch> is a literal. Nothing substitutes it, so the command asks GitHub for PRs whose head branch is named <branch> -- of which there are none -- and returns false for every possible state of the world, including the healthy one."

Same file (skills/commander/templates/COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json), same postcondition (archive.c2b), same unsubstituted token, and both proved it the same way: run the command once with the literal and once with the real branch.

SUGGESTED FIXES DIVERGE, which does not break the collapse: #439 asks for a resolver token added to init_work_area.py's _RESOLVER_OWNED_TOKEN_RE, resolved "at spine instantiation time"; #484 offers either that or a self-deriving command that "needs no substitution machinery". Carried to q9.

IMPORTANT: both bodies state the same WRONG mechanism for the failure -- "matches no real branch and always returns an empty list" / "asks GitHub for PRs whose head branch is named <branch>". Neither is what happens. See q4: gh is never reached.

q3-446-distinct.title: Is #446 a third issue on the same postcondition but a DISTINCT defect?
q3-446-distinct.imperative: The launch order asserts #439+#484+#446 are all archive.c2b and that c2b carries TWO defects. Confirm from #446's body that its defect (OPEN-only state criterion) is independent of the <branch> substitution defect, so that fixing one would not fix the other.
q3-446-distinct.finding:
DISTINCT DEFECT on the same postcondition -- confirmed from #446's body, which never mentions <branch> at all.

#446 body: "The archive postcondition c2b only accepts a PR in state OPEN. A merged PR fails it. Since no override_policy exists on that condition, a plain waive was refused, and the Commander had to pass --force to get past a gate it had satisfied better than the gate's own criterion required." And: "The gate is asking 'is there a PR carrying this work?' and answering it with 'is there an open PR?' Those come apart in exactly the success case."

Independence proven by construction: substituting the branch leaves --state open intact, so cmdr-420-engine-channel's already-merged PR still fails; and accepting MERGED leaves the literal <branch> intact, so every run still fails. Neither fix subsumes the other.

Provenance differs too. #446 was hit by a Commander whose PR the Admiral had ALREADY MERGED -- the normal epic division of labour -- whereas #439 and #484 were both hit with an OPEN PR live (#438 and #483 respectively).

So archive.c2b carries exactly two defects, as the launch order states.

q4-command-check-semantics.title: How does the engine decide a `command` postcondition passed — exit code only, or output?
q4-command-check-semantics.imperative: Load-bearing for fix C. `gh pr list ... --jq 'length > 0'` exits 0 while PRINTING `false`. If the engine reads exit code only, the SHIPPED c2b is a check that cannot FAIL, not one that cannot pass — which would contradict the reports in #439/#446 that it failed live. Read scripts/checklist_engine.py (read-only) and settle it.
q4-command-check-semantics.finding:
SETTLED, and it changes fix C. The engine's verdict on a command postcondition is RETURNCODE-ONLY.

scripts/checklist_engine.py:831-832 (read-only; crew 4 owns the file):
    proc, shell_marker = _run_check_command(chk["command"])
    cond["satisfied"] = proc.returncode == 0
Nothing reads stdout. The comment above it says so in its own words: "the engine's own verdict here is returncode-only".

So the printed word "false" is invisible to the engine. Two consequences, both measured just now in this worktree:

(1) WHY THE SHIPPED CHECK ACTUALLY FAILS is not what either issue says. The engine runs the check text through sh -c. In sh, the unquoted "<" in "--head <branch>" is an INPUT REDIRECTION, not an argument:
    $ sh -c "gh pr list --head <branch> --state open --json number --jq 'length > 0'"
    sh: line 1: branch: No such file or directory
    exit=1
gh is never invoked at all. The check fails because the shell cannot open a file named "branch". #439 says it "matches no real branch and always returns an empty list" and #484 says it "asks GitHub for PRs whose head branch is named <branch>"; neither happens. The observable verdict (red) is right and both diagnoses of the mechanism are wrong.

(2) THE OBVIOUS FIX WOULD MOVE THE DEFECT, NOT REMOVE IT. Substitute a real branch and keep --jq 'length > 0':
    $ sh -c "gh pr list --head 'no-such-branch-xyz' --state open --json number --jq 'length > 0'"
    false
    exit=0
Exit 0. Under returncode-only, the engine marks that SATISFIED. So substituting the branch and keeping the shipped jq expression converts a check that cannot pass into a check that CANNOT FAIL -- green whether or not any PR exists. This is exactly the defect class epic #418 exists to remove, and #484's own suggested replacement command ("gh pr list --head "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" --state open --json number --jq 'length > 0'") walks straight into it.

CONSTRAINT ON FIX C, therefore: the replacement command must EXIT NONZERO when no qualifying PR exists. A boolean-printing jq expression will not do; the count must be compared in the shell (e.g. test "$(... --jq 'length')" -gt 0) or the boolean matched exactly.

q5-fixA-blockers.title: How many distinct clauses must change before a `stop` boundary can close execute.c3?
q5-fixA-blockers.imperative: #506 records three successive refusals. Pre-ruling 1 names only the authorization clause. Read verify_admiral_prelaunch and _next_wave and enumerate BY CODE every clause a decision=stop packet fails, so the chosen shape is not a partial fix that leaves the gate still unclosable.
q5-fixA-blockers.finding:
TWO clauses in this file block a decision=stop packet, not one. Pre-ruling 1 names only the second, so its shape as literally written is a partial fix.

Enumerated by walking verify_admiral_prelaunch (scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py:132-156) with decision=stop:

BLOCKER 1 -- _next_wave(), line 115: _string(value["launch_id"], ...) requires a NONEMPTY string. A stop authorizes no launch, so the artifact cannot even express the state. #506 hit this first: "NEXT_WAVE.launch_id = null -> REFUSED: Admiral NEXT_WAVE.launch_id must be a nonempty string". #506's own option 2 is exactly this clause ("Today the artifact cannot even express a stop").

BLOCKER 2 -- line 145-148: _require(result["decision"] in {"advance", "replan"}, "only advance or replan may authorize NEXT_WAVE"). This is the clause pre-ruling 1 names.

Everything else on the path is already stop-clean, verified by reading each:
 - _next_wave trigger set {wave_boundary, material_exception}: a stop at a wave boundary is wave_boundary. Not a blocker.
 - verify_replan_result (G2): the installed replan verifier's DECISIONS set is {"advance","repair","replan","stop"} (verify_replan.py:22) and line 313 explicitly contemplates stop ("only stop may set result.current_wave to null"). G2 accepts a stop.
 - result["applicable"] is True (line 144): applicable is a free boolean at G2 (verify_replan.py:305); a stop can be applicable.
 - _verify_transition_audit: TRANSITION_LINE's decision group is [^ |]+, so decision=stop matches. Proven against the live epic: .agent-work/epic-418-redux/ADMIRAL_LOG.md:3242 carries "- TRANSITION | boundary=w4-to-close | decision=stop | verified".
 - render_replan_markdown and the CURRENT_TRUTH/WAVE_REVIEW writes: decision-agnostic.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SHAPE: fixing only the authorization clause leaves the gate still unclosable, because launch_id would still have to be a nonempty lie. #506's options 1 and 2 are therefore not alternatives -- option 1 needs option 2 to work at all.

Also noted, NOT changed: decision=repair is refused by the same clause. #506 is scoped to stop and says so; widening authorization to repair would change what may launch a wave, which is not this run's question.

q6-fixA-shape.title: Which of #506's three shapes does fix A take?
q6-fixA-shape.imperative: Pre-ruling 1 pre-rules the conditional shape and permits the other two with a stated argument. Resolve against the launch order, not by preference; record the ruling verbatim as the answer.
q6-fixA-shape.finding:
RESOLVED FROM THE LAUNCH ORDER, pre-ruling 1, quoted verbatim:

"Fix A's shape -- c3 becomes conditional on there being a launch. When REPLAN_RESULT.decision is stop, the closure check verifies the transition is *recorded, G2-verified and rendered* and skips the authorization clause. The audit value is in the packet, not in the launch. The two alternatives (launch_id: null becomes legal for stop; or a separate admiral-boundary mode) are both acceptable if you argue for them -- pick one and say why."

TAKEN: option 1, NECESSARILY COMBINED WITH option 2, and NOT option 3.

Option 1 alone is not implementable -- q5 shows a stop packet is refused by _next_wave's nonempty-launch_id clause before the authorization clause is ever reached. So "launch_id: null becomes legal for stop" is not an alternative to the conditional shape; it is the part of it that lets the artifact express a stop at all. I take both, which is what pre-ruling 1's own sentence "conditional on there being a launch" requires in code.

Option 3 (a separate admiral-boundary mode) is DECLINED, with the reason: execute.c3 in ADMIRAL_SPINE.template.json invokes the mode by name ("verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py admiral-prelaunch --work-id <work-id>"), so a new mode name forces an edit to the admiral spine template, which this run's File Ownership does not grant it (q11). Keeping the mode name and making it decision-aware delivers the same separation of questions entirely inside a file this run owns.

The launch order's Inherited Latitude grants the implementation shape inside the pre-rulings ("You may: choose the implementation shape inside the pre-rulings"), so no float is required for this.

q7-fixB-discriminator.title: What structural fact separates an installed bundle from a source checkout?
q7-fixB-discriminator.imperative: Pre-ruling 4 forbids widening the guard. Find a fact that is TRUE in the installed world and FALSE in the repo world, verified on disk in both, so the replacement guard can still fail. Test every candidate against both roots.
q7-fixB-discriminator.finding:
Three structural facts were tested on disk against all three real worlds. All three discriminate; the name test does not.

Measured (python, both roots, this session):

  world = INSTALLED bundle  ~/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral
    name.startswith("constellation-")            True
    skill_root/SKILL.md is_file                  True
    parent/CORPUS.json is_file                   True
    parent/constellation-replan/scripts/verify_replan.py is_file   True
    derived skills_root                          C:\Users\fredc\.claude\skills

  world = SOURCE repo, main checkout  C:/Programs/constellation-skills
    name.startswith("constellation-")            True   <-- the defect
    skill_root/SKILL.md is_file                  False
    parent/CORPUS.json is_file                   False
    parent/constellation-replan/... is_file      False
    derived skills_root                          C:\Programs

  world = SOURCE repo, WORKTREE  C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/epic418-w5-gates
    name.startswith("constellation-")            False
    skill_root/SKILL.md is_file                  False
    parent/CORPUS.json is_file                   False
    derived skills_root                          C:\Programs\constellation-skills-wt

CHOSEN DISCRIMINATOR: an installed bundle is a directory that carries its own SKILL.md AND whose parent is a skills root -- where "is a skills root" is itself structural (carries the installer's CORPUS.json marker, or carries at least one constellation-*/SKILL.md sibling). Both halves are needed: SKILL.md alone would accept skills/<name>/ inside the source repo, whose parent (skills/) is not a skills root.

Why not the name: it answers "is this directory called constellation-something", which is true in both worlds. Why SKILL.md + skills-root: the installer is what creates that shape (README, "Repo layout vs. installed layout": install bundles "each skill's SKILL.md, its scripts/, references/, and templates/ into a self-contained folder named constellation-<name>/ under the agent's skills root", and "Every install stamps a CORPUS.json provenance marker at the skills root"). It is the marker the installer writes, which is the shape #468 asked for.

THIRD MANIFESTATION FOUND, in neither issue: from a Commander WORKTREE the current guard refuses outright, because a worktree directory is not named constellation-*. Reproduced live:
  $ py scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py admiral-prelaunch --work-id epic-418-redux   (run in the worktree)
  REFUSED: role verifier must run from an installed constellation-* skill
  exit=1
COMMANDER_SPINE's own execute.c2 runs "python scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py commander --work-id <work-id>" from exactly there. So this guard makes execute.c2 a check that cannot pass in EVERY commander worktree, including this run's. It is the same defect wearing the opposite sign: in the main checkout the guard wrongly PASSES, in a worktree it wrongly REFUSES, and neither answer is about whether an installed corpus is reachable.

q8-fixB-refuse-or-resolve.title: Should the vendored copy REFUSE with a better message, or RESOLVE the real skills root?
q8-fixB-refuse-or-resolve.imperative: #468's acceptance asks for a message naming the real cause. #501's acceptance asks that the repo-checkout invocation SUCCEED (or the imperative be corrected). These are different fixes. Resolve against the launch order and against the consequence for the Commander spine's own execute.c2, which invokes the vendored copy from a worktree.
q8-fixB-refuse-or-resolve.finding:
RESOLVED FROM THE LAUNCH ORDER: BOTH, in that order -- resolve when an installed corpus is genuinely reachable, refuse with a message naming the real problem when it is not.

Launch order pre-ruling 4, verbatim: "Fix B must not widen the guard into a check that cannot fail. 'Accept the repo checkout too' makes the guard pass everywhere, which is worse than today. The guard's job is to answer *where am I running from* -- make it answer that (e.g. detect an installed bundle by its structure, not by its name) and give the refusal a message that names the real problem, per #468."

The pre-ruling forbids one specific widening -- accepting the repo checkout AS an installed bundle, i.e. keeping the wrong derived root and calling it fine. It does not forbid answering the question honestly ("I am NOT an installed bundle") and then locating the installed corpus separately. Those are different mechanisms: the first destroys the discriminator, the second keeps it and adds a resolution step behind it.

Deciding argument, from the two issues' own acceptance criteria, which pull in different directions:
 - #468 acceptance: "running the vendored copy from this repo produces a message naming the actual cause, and ... the check is observed refusing rather than only observed passing."
 - #501 acceptance: "The invocation named in the Admiral spine's execute imperative runs successfully from the repo checkout, or the imperative is corrected to name the installed copy."
A refusal-only fix satisfies #468 and fails #501. Correcting the imperative instead is not available for the admiral spine (not this run's file, q11).

The consequence settles it. COMMANDER_SPINE's execute.c2 invokes the vendored copy from a worktree (q7). A refusal-only fix would leave that postcondition permanently red for every Commander -- shipping a brand-new check-that-cannot-pass into the epic whose subject is checks that cannot pass, and forcing a waiver on every run. That is the failure mode pre-ruling 6 forbids creating.

SHAPE: (1) explicit --skills-root wins if given; (2) else, if this file sits in an installed bundle by the q7 structural test, use its parent; (3) else probe the known user-scope skills roots in a fixed order and take the first that structurally IS a skills root AND carries the sibling verifiers this script loads, printing a visible note on stderr that it is running outside an installed bundle and which root it resolved (a stated fallback, not a hidden one); (4) else REFUSE, naming the real problem and every root tried.

It can still fail, which is the point: step 4 is reachable, and --skills-root pointed anywhere wrong reaches it too. That is the mutation test #501's acceptance demands ("point the resolver at a wrong root and the acceptance check must go red").

q9-fixC-substitution-mechanism.title: Resolver token at instantiation, or a self-deriving command at check time?
q9-fixC-substitution-mechanism.imperative: #439 asks for a resolver token; #484 offers the self-deriving form. Establish first, as a FACT, whether the branch is guaranteed to exist at spine-instantiation time — the init imperative's own ordering settles it. Then resolve the mechanism against the launch order's latitude.
q9-fixC-substitution-mechanism.finding:
SELF-DERIVING AT CHECK TIME, not a resolver token at instantiation.

The prior fact that decides it: the branch is NOT guaranteed to exist when the spine is instantiated. init's own imperative orders the two acts in this sequence -- "use it to instantiate spine.json rather than hand-substituting placeholders ... Start the work branch per repo guidance." Spine instantiation comes first; branch creation comes after. A token frozen at instantiation therefore captures whatever branch the worktree happened to be on -- for a Commander that branches after scaffolding, that is main. The check would then ask whether a PR exists for main, which is a different question that can be answered "yes" by an unrelated PR. That is a worse failure than the current one, because it is green.

This run is not a counter-example: this worktree was provisioned onto epic-418/w5-bookend-gates before init ran, so a frozen token would have been correct HERE and wrong for the general case. That is precisely the shape of a check that passes in the one world you tested it in.

Two further reasons: a Commander that renames or re-bases its branch mid-run silently invalidates a frozen value; and #484 records the same conclusion from the other side -- the self-deriving form "needs no substitution machinery and works from any worktree".

MECHANISM: the check derives the branch itself, pinned to the run's root through the resolver token that already exists rather than inheriting the launcher's cwd:
    git -C <repo-root> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
<repo-root> is already resolver-owned (init_work_area.py:29, resolved at line 148 with as_posix()), so this needs no new token family and no change to _RESOLVER_OWNED_TOKEN_RE. It also closes the cwd fragility that #341 tracks separately, for this check.

ACCEPTED DIVERGENCE, to be reported, not hidden: #439's acceptance item 1 reads "<branch> resolves to the real current branch at spine instantiation". That literal criterion is NOT met -- the token is removed from the template instead, so there is nothing left to resolve. Its other two acceptance items are met (c2b passes without --force on a real run; regression test added). Reported as fixed-by-different-means with the ordering hazard above as the reason.

The launch order's Inherited Latitude grants the implementation shape inside the pre-rulings; pre-ruling 5 constrains the OUTCOME ("The gate is asking is there a PR carrying this work -- answer that question") and not the mechanism.

q10-fixC-state-criterion.title: What PR states must c2b accept?
q10-fixC-state-criterion.imperative: #446 asks for OPEN plus MERGED and explicitly excludes CLOSED-unmerged. Confirm the state vocabulary `gh pr list --json state` actually emits, by running it, before writing a filter against invented values.
q10-fixC-state-criterion.finding:
ACCEPT {OPEN, MERGED}; REJECT CLOSED-unmerged. The state vocabulary was read off the forge, not assumed.

  $ gh pr view 438 --json number,state,headRefName
    {"headRefName":"epic-418/d-422-wire-invariants","number":438,"state":"MERGED"}     <- #439's own PR
  $ gh pr view 483 --json number,state,headRefName
    {"headRefName":"epic-418/b-433-render-directives","number":483,"state":"CLOSED"}   <- #484's own PR
  $ gh pr list --head epic-418/b-420-engine-channel --state all --json number,state,headRefName
    [{"number":435,"state":"MERGED"},{"number":434,"state":"MERGED"}]                  <- #446's own run

gh emits exactly OPEN / CLOSED / MERGED, and MERGED is a distinct value rather than CLOSED plus a flag, so a single select on state is sufficient. #446's requirement quoted: "Accept state in {OPEN, MERGED} for c2b. A CLOSED-but-unmerged PR should still fail, since that genuinely means the work did not land."

The candidate command, run against four real branches covering all three states plus no-PR-at-all, with the count compared in the shell so the exit code carries the verdict (q4):

  test "$(gh pr list --head "$(git -C <repo-root> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" --state all --json state --jq '[.[] | select(.state == "OPEN" or .state == "MERGED")] | length')" -gt 0

  epic-418/w5-bookend-gates        no PR yet        exit=1   (correctly red)
  epic-418/d-422-wire-invariants   MERGED  (#438)   exit=0   (the #439 case)
  epic-418/b-433-render-directives CLOSED  (#483)   exit=1   (correctly red -- work did not land)
  epic-418/b-420-engine-channel    MERGED  (#435)   exit=0   (the #446 case, which previously forced --force)

It is observed both passing and failing on real inputs, which is what the two-worlds requirement asks for. Note #446's second-order cost is visible in that last row: two merged PRs on one branch, the extra one filed "purely to carry closeout bookkeeping past the gate".

q11-ownership-admiral-spine.title: Does fix A require editing a file outside this run's ownership?
q11-ownership-admiral-spine.imperative: execute.c3 lives in the ADMIRAL spine template, which the launch order lists neither as mine nor as another crew's. Determine by reading the admiral spine template whether the chosen fix-A shape can be delivered entirely inside scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py. If it cannot, that is a float, not a decision.
q11-ownership-admiral-spine.finding:
NO -- the chosen fix-A shape is deliverable entirely inside scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py, which this run owns. No float needed.

Read from skills/admiral/templates/ADMIRAL_SPINE.template.json, execute.c3:
  statement: "NEXT_WAVE names a boundary whose exact transition is uniquely audit-recorded, G2-verified, repair-safe, and rendered before launch"
  check: {"kind": "command", "command": "python <admiral-skill-dir>/scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py admiral-prelaunch --work-id <work-id>"}

The template names the script and the MODE STRING. So long as the mode keeps the name admiral-prelaunch and the flag surface is unchanged, the template needs no edit and the fix lands wholly in this run's file. That is the concrete reason option 3 (a separate admiral-boundary mode) is declined in q6 -- it would require renaming the mode at the call site.

Ownership as the launch order states it: "Yours alone this wave: scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py, skills/commander/templates/COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json, scripts/init_work_area.py, and their tests." The admiral spine template appears in neither the mine list nor the explicitly-not-mine list, so a shape needing it would be genuinely ambiguous. Choosing the shape that does not need it removes the ambiguity rather than resolving it by assumption.

q12-freshness-scope.title: Is #501's boundary-freshness guard in scope for this run?
q12-freshness-scope.imperative: #501 raises a second defect — NEXT_WAVE.json persists from the previous boundary, so a prelaunch check run early re-validates the boundary that already passed and reports ok. It appears in Suggested Fix but NOT in Acceptance. Resolve in or out against the launch order, and if in, choose a shape that adds no unused machinery.
q12-freshness-scope.finding:
OUT OF SCOPE for implementation this run -- recorded as a triage candidate with a falsification, not silently dropped. This is an honest null on a sub-part, per the launch order's Honest-Null Clause.

The ask, from #501's Suggested Fix item 3 (NOT in its Acceptance): "Suggest the prelaunch check refuse when NEXT_WAVE.json's boundary_id names a transition it has already verified, or require the caller to pass the expected boundary_id and refuse on mismatch."

I designed and then FALSIFIED the stateless variant before writing it. Candidate: refuse when NEXT_WAVE.boundary_id is not the LAST verified TRANSITION in ADMIRAL_LOG.md. Checked against the reported scenario using the live epic's own artifacts:

  .agent-work/epic-418-redux/ADMIRAL_LOG.md verified TRANSITION lines, in file order:
    w1-to-w2 replan (:327), w2-to-w3 replan (:465), w3-to-w4 replan (:969),
    w4-to-close stop (:3242), close-to-w5 advance (:3437)
  NEXT_WAVE.json: {"boundary_id": "close-to-w5", "launch_id": "w5-gates-readiness-and-cheap-fixes", "trigger": "material_exception"}

In the #501 scenario the operator runs the check BEFORE writing the new boundary. At that moment the stale NEXT_WAVE names the previous boundary -- and the previous boundary is also the last logged TRANSITION, because the new one has not been logged yet. The guard is green in exactly the world it was written to catch. It is a check that cannot fail, and I would have shipped one into the epic about checks that cannot fail.

The reason is structural: staleness is a mismatch between the artifact and the CALLER'S INTENT, and the caller's intent is in no artifact. So #501's second variant is the only sound one -- the caller passes the expected boundary_id -- and it is inert unless the call site passes it. The call site is ADMIRAL_SPINE.template.json's execute.c3, which this run does not own (q11). Building the flag now ships unused machinery, against the inherited "one canonical path; no speculative abstraction".

A second, weaker reason to defer: fix A makes admiral-prelaunch decision-aware, which changes what a stale read even means on the stop path. A freshness rule written before that lands would be written against the old shape.

ROUTED: recommend-and-defer at the triage step, carrying this falsification, so the next actor does not re-derive the dead variant. #501's stated Acceptance is fully met without it (q1).

zc-consolidate.title: Consolidate behind the finish gate
zc-consolidate.imperative: Do NOT record this until joint understanding is reached. Write the interrogation record from templates/INTERROGATION_RECORD.template.json (each question typed fact|decision; each resolved decision carrying its human_answer; each resolved fact its code_evidence) and capture the counterpart's explicit sign-off. Run `py scripts/verify_interrogation.py .agent-work/w5-gates/INTERROGATION_RECORD.json` — it MUST exit 0. Record pass only after exit 0, then `consolidate`.

postconditions.statement: verify_interrogation.py exits 0 on the interrogation record -- refuses a self-answered decision or a consolidation with no joint-understanding sign-off

zc-consolidate.finding: INTERROGATION_RECORD.json written; verify_interrogation.py exits 0 (mode=delegated, questions=12, consolidated=True). All 12 questions resolved: 8 facts with code evidence, 4 decisions each carrying the launch-order section that answered it.

consolidation.summary:
Three fixes, all inside files this run owns, plus three findings that change what the issues asked for.

FIX A (#506) -- admiral-prelaunch becomes decision-aware, keeping its mode name. A stop packet is blocked by TWO clauses, not the one pre-ruling 1 names: launch_id must be a nonempty string, and decision must be in {advance, replan}. So #506's options 1 and 2 are not alternatives -- option 1 needs option 2 to be implementable. Under decision=stop the artifact may now express "no launch authorized" and the authorization clause is skipped, while G2 validation, the unique audit-entry match, the render and the CURRENT_TRUTH/WAVE_REVIEW writes all still run. Option 3 declined: a new mode name would force an edit to ADMIRAL_SPINE.template.json, which this run does not own. Mutation test on the stop path is required and not overridable.

FIX B (#501 + #468) -- the guard stops asking "am I called constellation-something" and asks "am I an installed bundle", structurally: this file's directory carries a SKILL.md AND its parent is a skills root (the installer's CORPUS.json marker, or a constellation-*/SKILL.md sibling). Verified on disk to be True for an installed bundle and False for both the main checkout and a worktree. When not installed, the script RESOLVES a real installed corpus (explicit --skills-root first, then a fixed probe order), printing a visible stderr note, and REFUSES with a message naming the real problem and every root tried when none is reachable. Refusal-only would satisfy #468 and fail #501, and would leave COMMANDER_SPINE execute.c2 permanently red.

FIX C (#439 + #484 + #446) -- archive.c2b is rewritten to derive its own branch through the existing <repo-root> token and to accept {OPEN, MERGED} while still rejecting CLOSED-unmerged, with the count compared in the shell so the exit code carries the verdict. No new resolver token: the branch may not exist when the spine is instantiated, because init's own imperative creates the branch after instantiating the spine.

DUPLICATE COLLAPSES, each confirmed against the issue BODY: #501/#468 hold on the primary defect, with #501 carrying one extra sub-ask that is deferred with a falsification; #439/#484 hold; #446 is a distinct defect on the same postcondition, and neither fix subsumes the other.

CARRIED UP: (1) the real failure mechanism of c2b is shell redirection, and the fix both issues suggest would produce a check that cannot fail; (2) the guard also breaks execute.c2 in every Commander worktree; (3) the boundary-freshness sub-ask is deferred with evidence that the stateless variant cannot discriminate.
